subsystem.name: VehicleAIAndPit
subsystem.responsibility: Vehicle AI decision state, AI command queue with duplicate detection, spatial nearest-neighbor queries, pairwise lateral interaction forces, front steering geometry, per-wheel tire slip forces, rigid-body constraint solving, and pit-stop machine behavior including the stall buffer and proximity contacts.

summary: This packet reconstructs the vehicle-AI and pit subsystem as a set of object classes and free-form frame-path computations. CommandQueue owns the AI command pair buffer (this+0x44A8, count this+0x44B0) and performs duplicate-command linear search. AIStateBuffer left-shifts two history buffers and sets four 0.5f weight fields plus an activation flag. AISpatialQuery delegates nearest-neighbor queries to the scene spatial tree (dword_5EA2C0). LateralForceModel computes pairwise proximity-weighted lateral interaction forces over the global vehicle pointer array (dword_7C54F0, count dword_5C329C) each frame. VehicleSteering performs front steering-geometry setup and angle computation from suspension-bar lookups. ConstraintSolver iterates 100-byte joint constraint records and 18-dword constraint elements, applies Gram-Schmidt projection, evaluates piecewise responses, and accumulates corrective impulses. TireSlipModel computes per-wheel slip forces, a longitudinal force modifier, and wheel-contact/particle effects on the frame path. F1CPitMachine holds the owner vehicle pointer and the pit-stop circular buffer (data 0x9B0, size 0x9B4, write index 0x9B8, read index 0x9BC), detects pit-stall proximity, and looks up teammate pit status by team ID (obj+0x48A4). SinglyLinkedList is a two-head list container with tail append; MilesAudioPollState, SteeringAssistTolerance, and FixedSizeContainer are small GUESS-owner helpers. SetContactConstraint, SteeringSensitivityInit, and AudioMixerGainInit remain owner-unknown. Ownership across the constraint methods is not independently proven; several raw vehicle-struct and a2-relative offsets are not part of the allowed evidence set and are described in unresolved only.

function_roles.role: Poll Miles audio sample playback status via AIL_sample_status; return the loop-mode flag (this+0x14) when the status is DONE(4) or STOPPED(16), otherwise return 2.
Linear search over the AI command queue's 8-byte {commandID,param} pairs for a duplicate command ID; return 1 on match else 0 for duplicate-command detection.

Delegate a spatial nearest-neighbor query: forward the object position and two search parameters to SpatialTreeNearestNeighborSearch on the scene spatial tree (dword_5EA2C0) with filter 0 and return the nearest-neighbor handle.

Compute pairwise proximity-weighted lateral interaction forces across all active vehicles (dword_7C54F0, count dword_5C329C) and write the resultant (x,0,z) vector into each vehicle at offset 14948; called per frame by MainGameTickUpdate.

Initialize the AI state buffer: left-shift two history buffers (0xC4- and 0xBC4-based, 64-byte stride), set four float fields at 0x1CA8-0x1CB4 to 0.5f, and set the activation byte at this+0x0 to 1; return 1056964608.
Store a per-entry wheel contact-constraint value (float slot at dword index a2+1841) and mark the entry active (byte flag at byte offset a2+7360); called during wheel-dynamics initialisation.

Solve rigid-body joint constraint records between two bodies: transform anchor directions, form position/angular deltas, apply corrective angular-momentum impulses, and return the number of records processed.

Constraint response step: compute displacement error from the reference value (this+0x1F8), write position (this+0x1E8) and velocity (this+0x1F0) error terms, evaluate PiecewiseFunctionEval, and store the response to a caller-derived output pointer.
Gram-Schmidt projection step: dot the reference constraint direction with the direction being orthogonalized, subtract the scaled projection, and return the dot product used as the projection factor.

Set up front steering geometry for both wheels: match suspension components by geometry id and name, apply the steering angle via a tan-based formula, and rebuild wheel rotation matrices; log an error when the eight components are missing.
Compute steering geometry for both front wheels from left/right steering suspension bars and fore upper/lower suspension points; store left/right steering angles at this+0x163C and this+0x1650.

Search the constraint element array (this+0x15C8, count this+0x15C4) for the element whose body-pair identifiers match this+0x15F0/this+0x141C, then accumulate the incoming delta and compute the constraint force for the matched element.
Compute per-wheel tire slip factors and force slots, a longitudinal force modifier, wheel-contact effects, and normalized per-wheel values on the frame path; called from the vehicle physics tick.
Initialize steering-sensitivity globals: write 0.0 to flt_7CCCB8 and 1065353216 to dword_7CCCBC.
Initialize audio mixer gain globals: write the decimal literal -1082130432 to dword_7CA488 and 0.0 to flt_7CA48C.
Initialize a six-dword global constraint-solver parameter block: store literal 45 into dword_7CCEB8 and zero dword_7CCEBC..dword_7CCECC; return 0.
Append a node to the tail of the singly-linked list rooted at this+0xCC, walking node next-pointers at node+0x18.
Append a node to the tail of the singly-linked list rooted at this+0xD4, walking node next-pointers at node+0x18; structural mirror of the sibling append helper.

Look up the team-mate vehicle's part value: scan the global vehicle pointer array dword_7C54F0 for a different vehicle with the same team ID (obj+0x48A4) and return its part value; called by ForcePitExit.
Pit-stall proximity check: query and lazily reinitialize the pit-stop circular buffer, walk entries backward from this+0x9B8, and register a collision contact when a stall is within reach.
Check whether an angular difference a2 is within a tolerance scaled by a difficulty/assist index (this+0x9AC) and an additional factor a3, using two switch-selected tolerance tables.

Append a new entry to the pit-stop circular buffer and write a float into its Z field (array this+0x9B0 + 176*writeIndex + 108), resetting the buffer via PhysicsObjectListManager when indices are invalid.

Construct a fixed-size element container: allocate 1016*count+4 bytes, store the count in the 4-byte header, and run an element initializer over each 1016-byte element; called by VehicleInstanceListBuilder.

classes.name: CommandQueue
classes.responsibility: Owns the AI command pair buffer and its count; supports duplicate-command detection through linear pair search.

classes.name: AIStateBuffer
classes.responsibility: Ring/history buffer for AI decision state: left-shifts two history buffers, holds four 0.5f weight fields, and carries an activation flag.

classes.name: AISpatialQuery
classes.responsibility: Provides nearest-neighbor queries against the scene spatial tree (dword_5EA2C0) on behalf of AI callers.

classes.name: LateralForceModel
classes.responsibility: Computes pairwise proximity-weighted lateral interaction forces across all active vehicles each frame and writes the resultant vector into each vehicle.

classes.name: VehicleSteering
classes.responsibility: Performs front steering-geometry setup and angle computation from suspension-bar and steering-data lookups.

classes.name: ConstraintSolver
classes.responsibility: Solves rigid-body joint and per-element constraints: world-space anchor resolution, Gram-Schmidt projection, error evaluation, and force/impulse accumulation.

classes.name: F1CPitMachine
classes.responsibility: Owns the vehicle pit-machine state: team lookup, pit-stop circular buffer, and pit-stall proximity contact registration.

classes.name: TireSlipModel
classes.responsibility: Computes per-wheel tire slip forces, a longitudinal force modifier, wheel-contact effects, and normalized per-wheel outputs on the frame path.

classes.name: SinglyLinkedList
classes.responsibility: Singly-linked list container with two heads (this+0xCC and this+0xD4); supports tail append via node next-pointers at node+0x18.

classes.name: MilesAudioPollState
classes.responsibility: Audio-sample playback status polling state used with the Miles AIL API.

classes.name: SteeringAssistTolerance
classes.responsibility: Difficulty-scaled steering-alignment tolerance check using two switch-selected tolerance tables.

classes.name: FixedSizeContainer
classes.responsibility: Fixed-size element container with a 4-byte header and 1016-byte elements.

interfaces.name: SpatialNearestNeighborQuery

compatibility_contracts.name: AICommandQueuePairLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The AI command queue holds 8-byte {commandID,param} pairs at this+0x44A8 with an entry count at this+0x44B0. A linear search over the pairs returns 1 when a pair's first dword equals the probe and 0 otherwise; the caller uses the result as a duplicate-command suppression signal.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitStopCircularBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The pit-stop buffer stores its data array at this+0x9B0, size at this+0x9B4, write index at this+0x9B8, and read index at this+0x9BC. Entries are 176 bytes and the float at entry+108 receives the pit-stop Z position. When the buffer indices are invalid, the data array is reinitialized via PhysicsObjectListManager.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitStallProximityContact
compatibility_contracts.description: PitStallProximityCheck walks the pit-stop stall buffer backward from the current index and registers a collision contact via CollisionObjectInsertion when the vehicle Z position is within 1.5 of a stall Z threshold.

compatibility_contracts.name: SpatialNearestNeighborQuery
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor queries resolve against the scene spatial tree at dword_5EA2C0 with filter 0 and return a nearest-neighbor handle, or zero when none is found.

compatibility_contracts.name: ConstraintElementArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The constraint element array lives at this+0x15C8 with count at this+0x15C4 and an 18-dword stride. Body-pair identifiers are matched at element+0x4 and element+0xC against this+0x15F0 and this+0x141C; constraint pointers are guarded at element+0x8 and element+0x10, and force components are written at element+0x20/+0x28/+0x30. The packet also reads element+0x10 as the output vector base, so its dual role is unresolved.

compatibility_contracts.name: BodyRotationMatrixLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The body rotation matrix reached via this+0x15F0 exposes rows used for constraint force computation at relative offsets +0x04..+0x5C, and the vehicle transform translation at +0x04/+0x0C/+0x14 with direction/cross vectors at +0x64..+0x8C used by tire effects.

compatibility_contracts.name: AudioSampleStatusContract
compatibility_contracts.description: AudioSampleStatusPoll returns the loop-mode flag at this+0x14 when the Miles sample status is 4 (DONE) or 16 (STOPPED), otherwise returns 2; the sample handle is read at this[0x58]+16.

unresolved: Ownership across the ConstraintSolver methods is not independently proven: 0x004359A0 reads a joint object (body A at this+0, records at this+0x98/0x9C), while 0x004380B0/0x00438930 read different field blocks (0x1E8-0x1F8, 0x15C/0x178-0x2B8) and 0x0043BA20 reads the element array at 0x15C4/0x15C8/0x15F0. The packet provides no proof they share one `this` object; they are grouped defensibly as one solver class.

this+0x15F0 is read both as a body identifier (DWORD) for element matching in 0x0043BA20 and as a pointer to the body/vehicle rotation matrix block in the same function and in 0x004472B0/0x0043B040/0x0043B590; whether these are the same value is unresolved.
The constraint element at +0x10 is guarded as a non-null constraint pointer AND written as the first element of the constraint output vector in 0x0043BA20; the packet itself is contradictory here.
In ConstraintForceSolver the element field at relative offset 0x38 (listed RW) is not written by this function; it may be written by RelativeVelocityCompute or sub_56D2D0.

SetContactConstraint (0x00431930) writes a float slot at dword index a2+1841 (byte 0x1CC4+4*a2) and a byte flag at byte offset a2+7360 (0x1CC0+a2); these parallel-array origins are outside the allowed evidence offsets, so no class fields are declared for them. The enclosing object layout and stride are unknown.
The four 0.5f fields at 0x1CA8-0x1CB4 in AIStateBuffer are interpreted as weights/confidence only by prior analysis; the packet does not establish their semantic meaning.
The element type and semantic meaning of the AIStateBuffer history buffers (64-byte stride) and of the FixedSizeContainer 1016-byte elements are not established.

LateralForceModel and TireSlipModel reach the vehicle struct through raw integer offsets (e.g. +13524/+13528/+13532/+13536/+13544/+13548/+13556/+13568/+13620/+13628/+14948 for lateral force; per-wheel table base unk_7C7810 with 1124-byte stride; AISpatialQuery position pointer at this+13536) that are not part of the allowed evidence set, so their semantic meaning rests on skeleton-fill prose only.

The packet-annotated constant-pool globals (dbl_59E420/dbl_59E428/dbl_59E430, flt_59E43C/flt_59E440, dbl_59E4E0, dbl_59E7E0, flt_59E7F8, flt_59E84C, dbl_59E880, flt_59E888, flt_59E8A4, flt_59E8A8, dbl_59E974, flt_59E9E0, flt_59E9E4, dbl_59EC10, dbl_59ECA8, dbl_59EEC0, dbl_59EEC8, flt_59EED0, dbl_59EED8, flt_59EEE0, dbl_59EEE8, flt_5ACD44, flt_5ACD58, flt_5ACD5C, flt_5ACD60, dword_8ACEA0) are reported read by the deterministic facts but appear nowhere in the raw decompiled source; they are presumed constant-pool operands, but the exact constant-to-global mapping is not established.

AudioMixerGainInit writes the decimal literal -1082130432 to dword_7CA488; interpreting it as an IEEE-754 or two's-complement bit pattern is prohibited by worker rules, so its numeric meaning is left as written.

RigidBodyConstraintJointSolver's summary names the physics integration step 0x00441D60 as a caller, but no caller:0x00441D60 reference is present in the allowed evidence set; this relationship is not asserted.
AIStateBufferInitialize is described as called by CleanupWrapper (0x00433EB0) in its summary, but no caller:0x00433EB0 reference is in the allowed evidence set; the caller is not asserted.

The exact mapping between the compiled double constants and the individual literals in VehicleSteering (1.0, 0.0, -0.5, reciprocal) and the semantics of a2+5168/a2+5176/a2+5184/a2+5188 steering factors are not recoverable from this packet.

Constraint record layout (type dword at base, direction at +4/+28, second anchor at +52, limit at +76, coefficients at +84/+92, 100-byte stride) and constraint type values other than 0 and 2 are inferred from field usage, not a known struct definition.
In ConstraintEnforce the raw source shows v4 as an uninitialized ecx register; the final output location at v4+516 (0x204) is not linked to a known field of `this`.
SteeringAlignmentToleranceCheck's field 0x9AC is a difficulty/assist index 0..3; its exact meaning and setter are not evidenced here, and the a3 factor semantics are caller-dependent.
The meaning of the return value 2 in AudioSampleStatusPoll (still playing or unknown status) is not grounded from the packet.

The list walk in the append helpers reads node next-pointers at node+0x18, but the packet's indirect base notation does not match the raw register-based traversal; the exact tail-node base is unproven. Whether the two heads (0xCC and 0xD4) belong to one object or two is unknown.
PitStallProximityCheck's first CircularBufferCheck call appears argument-less in the decompiler output; whether it also receives `this` is unclear.

SteeringSensitivityInit (0x0044C9F4), AudioMixerGainInit (0x0044CF94), and SetContactConstraint (0x00431930) have no confirmed owning class; the exact runtime roles of flt_7CCCB8/dword_7CCCBC and dword_7CA488/flt_7CA48C are not evidenced beyond the writes.
The teammate part value at obj+0x3450 read by TeammatePartValueLookup is not part of the allowed evidence offsets; its semantics are inferred from existing analysis only.
No state machines are evidenced by this packet; state_machines is empty by design.

The read-only constant-pool globals are also listed in unresolved_evidence_refs because the packet flags them as never appearing by name in the raw source; their placement in function evidence is attribution, not confirmation of constant identity.
